global: Vertical explainer Short about tracking a fast target with a space telescope: off-white canvas, black line art, thin grey construction lines, red for the tracking ray, wedge and rate labels; presenter-and-board opening; a DARK_FIELD starfield with a white line-art telescope, a grey Earth and a Moon; split-panel 'MANUAL TRACKING' scene with a divider; EXPECTATION/REALITY comparison; blurred photographic inset in a speech bubble; black REDACTED silhouette at the end.
motion: Mostly 1-frame pops and hard cuts; text typed (TOO SLOW, 3 f) and arrows/dashed lines drawn on (4-11 f); whole-canvas slides/pans with motion blur (G0010, G0012, G0018, ~8-17 f); a slow ~60-f drift of the telescope with a ghost copy left behind; a stepwise ~60-f telescope rotation with the red ray swinging to the Moon; a 6-f label fade-in (TOO CLOSE); a 2-frame colour-inverted negative flash on the right panel after a CLICK label; a 6-f cross-dissolve EXPECTATION->REALITY; speech bubble scales up over 9 f; a camera zoom into the bubble (16 f) and a long blurred-photo rotation then zoom-out (77 f).
continuity: The telescope drawing (same panels, antenna, aperture door) is reused at every scale; a grey ghost copy marks the previous pose; the Moon is a small grey disc on a grey horizontal line; red always means the pointing ray and its angular rate; the divider line splits 'MANUAL TRACKING' (left) from the diagram (right). Do not reuse the agency logo, the third-party astronomy photographs or the national flag.
